recipes.name: Cream Cheese Alfredo Sauce
ingredients_raw: 6 ounces grated Parmesan cheese, or to taste

steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in mushrooms; cook and stir until softened, about 5 minutes. Set aside.
Melt cream cheese and 1/2 cup butter in a saucepan, stirring occasionally, over medium heat. Stir in milk and Parmesan cheese until smooth.
Add basil, garlic, and white pepper. Simmer until flavors blend, about 5 minutes; stir in mushrooms.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream Cheese Alfredo Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This homemade Alfredo sauce with cream cheese and sautéed mushrooms is easy to make for a smooth, creamy white pasta sauce, perfect for fettuccini.

review.reviewBody: AWESOME and EASY! I used an 8oz. pkg. of sliced mushrooms, because that's all I had, which I sauteed in the 1/2 cup of butter (omitting the 2 tbsps.). Then I added in a clove of minced garlic (which I left in there). Once that was done, I added in the block of cream cheese and melted it in. I then added in the milk and combined until smooth. I added the parm to thicken and at the end, I added a box of frozen peas that I had cooked. Heated it all through and seasoned with pepper and a little dried basil (it's all I had)...YUM, YUM, YUM!!!! I served this over wagon wheel shaped pasta for something fun. I LOVED the ease of this recipe, and the outcome was nothing short of DELICIOUS! The beauty of this recipe is that it is so versatile and pretty much anything you like can be added. I will definately be making this often (I'm an alfredo addict, lol)! Thanks for sharing. :)

I have been making this recipe for years (given to me by a friend). I use Chicken or Shrimp instead of the mushrooms, or make it plain. However, I DO NOT use the butter at all. It does not need it and is still SO GOOD. That really cuts down the fat content and almost makes it a healthy recipe!

This is perfect for home cooked alfredo sauce! I cut down the butter amount to just 2tbsp. If your sauce ever turns out to be too think and you want to cut down on calories, try addding chicken stock instead of milk to thin it. Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe!

LOVE THIS RECIPE!! I was apprehensive at first. But, after I made it. I was ecstatic over the flavor!! Ok, as with everyone else. I made some changes. After reading some of the reviews I did these 2 things: #1.) I used/substituted regular Cream Cheese with GARLIC & HERB Cream Cheese. #2.) I reduced the butter by just a little bit. Instead of a whole stick of butter (1/2 cup), I used between 1/4 to 3/4 stick of butter. and that is it! It was creamy. It was rich. And I will definitely make it again.! 


I made a Lobster & Shrimp alfredo. So I made the sauce. Then I used my Traeger grill and smoked the shrimp and lobster for 20 minutes. then I combined them with the sauce. I let the sauce simmer for another15 - 20 minutes and serve!

Loved this recipe as it was super easy, and it tastes totally delicious!! 

I did make a few changes....
-used white mushrooms instead of portobello. 
-cooked sliced mushrooms in the 1/2 cup butter (omitting the 2 tbsp)
-added cream cheese to the mushrooms. 
- then added garlic and left it in
- added approx 1/2 cup white wine in the end (adds wonderful flavour while making the sauce a bit thin to make it go a longer way)

I will never buy jarred Alfredo sauce again. This recipe is the best I ve used. Other alfredo recipes called for a flour roux and I had issues trying to get a tasty sauce using this method. Resorted back to puchasing jarred., however, never again. I used approx. Lb of fresh spinach with the mushrooms and butter. Scooted this mixture to the side and then added cream cheese, milk and parm cheese. One skillet!! I used rotini pasta and it may have worked better than noodles. Spinach and sauce attached to the spiral pasta

This was delicious! I used shredded Asiago, and it was awesome! I will make it next time with Parmesan just to compare, but I am sure it will be equally great. SO fast and easy! The best alfredo sauce I've made to date, and I've tried several on here. Thanks for sharing!

This recipe was easy peasy. We sauteed the mushrooms with minced garlic as well as used freeze dried basil. We also put the sauce over cheese ravioli. Don't get freaked out of sauce isn't totally smooth. Just don't under stir. Tasty vittles.
It was good and easy!! I used garlic powder, dried basil and 1/2 of the butter and it turn out great.

I reduced the butter in the melted cream cheese sauce to 2 tblspns. I left in the garlic, added dried basil and some dried parsley. I sauted the mushrooms with 1/2 red onion, one diced fancy large radish. I poured the sauce mix over brussel sprouts that I had preboiled until tender, slicing some in half. The mushrooms were really good in it, (crimini sliced, 6 oz) as was the radish. I then baked it for a little bit while the ham was finishing off, and never added the extra parmesan, it was tasty without it. Delish.

Whole family loved it. I added sauteed chicken and fresh spinach and eliminated the mushrooms. I cut butter to 2 Tblsp and didn't miss it at all. I also added a teaspoon of cooking sherry. Quick and easy. If it's too thick, I sometimes add a bit of chicken broth.
loved it! never will I buy another jar of the sauce again

Adjustments: less butter, pasta water instead of milk, more cheese. The tang of the cream cheese made me think to add lemon juice which was great. So no, not the recipe as written, but the cream cheese is a great base for a quick sauce.

This was a nice easy recipe to make. I used the whipped version of philly cream cheese, because that is what I had, and it worked and blended very nicely. I added two frozen nuggets of spinach which I brought to room temp for a couple hours on the counter and drained. The family enjoyed the meal :) I will make again.
Best sauce ever! It will be our go-to for everything. I made it for pizza and it was delicious! Can’t wait to try it on other things!

Tastes pretty good and came together easily, mine was a little runny so I ended up adding 1.5 tbsp of flour at the end to thicken it. I added spinach to it as well which might have been why mine was runny, and also why it is green. Overall good recipe!

Melting the cream cheese and butter together did not work. The mixture got super lumpy and stayed that way. The bits of cream cheese were very rubbery and would not mix in with the butter, even after repeated whisking. I couldn't even complete the recipe, as it was not salvageable.

Absolutely delicious, the nicest pasta dish I've ever made. I added a little water and chicken stock to the mix for a bit of saltiness. It was perfect and today, a cold windy day in a South African game reserve, I'm making it again.
